In linguistics , a calque ( / k æ l k / ) or loan translation is a word or phrase borrowed from another language by literal word-for-word or root-for-root translation . When used as a verb , "to calque" means to borrow a word or phrase from another language while translating its components, so as to create a new word or phrase ( lexeme ) in the target language. For instance, the English word skyscraper has been calqued in dozens of other languages, [ 1 ] combining words for "sky" (or "clouds") and "scrape" in each language, such as wolkenkrabber in Dutch.
